clue.text: Feeling sorry that Tory's hackneyed

parts.note: CON is the abbreviation for Conservative, a Tory
hackneyed and trite both mean overused and stale

explanation.surface: Someone regrets that a Conservative politician is stale and unoriginal.
explanation.definitionFit: A contrite person is penitent, full of remorse for a wrong they have done.

clue.text: Rotter in American agency is a six footer

indicators.note: in places the word for rotter within the abbreviation for the agency

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
a cad or rotter is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A tall villain inside the CIA is described as six feet tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six footer' suggests a tall person, but it means a creature with six legs, an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicada is a chirping insect, and all insects walk on six legs.

clue.text: Number in film in New York

indicators.note: the second in tells us the pair before it sits inside the abbreviation for the city

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York
taken as written
E.T. is Spielberg's film about an extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: A musical number appearing in a film set in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: E.T. is the Spielberg film, the go-to film in crosswords; the second 'in' is the instruction to place inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninety is a cardinal number, nine tens.

clue.text: Read about saint, certain to have doubts removed

definitions.note: the answer is a past participle: having had doubts removed

indicators.note: about means going around, so the first word wraps around what follows

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for saint
sure and certain are synonyms

explanation.surface: Someone reads up on a saint, sure that their doubts will be dispelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Read' looks like the verb of the sentence but is just the outer letters to wrap around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reassured means having one's fears or doubts put to rest by comfort or evidence.

clue.text: Men of the cloth with cards displayed by mannequins

definitions.note: the clue word is plural; the answer is singular

parts.note: jocular: men who work with cloth, rather than clergymen
in bridge the dummy is the hand laid face up on the table

explanation.surface: Clergymen playing cards shown off by shop-window models.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men of the cloth' normally means clergy; here the cloth is literal fabric. In bridge, the declarer's partner's cards are laid out openly and called the dummy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor's dummy is a model torso on which clothes are fitted or displayed, a kind of mannequin.

clue.text: Picture of small bits of the lawmaker's code

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an image made of small pieces of tile or glass
second meaning: relating to Moses, the lawgiver of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A picture made of fragments of a legislator's statute book.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mosaic law is the law handed down by Moses, so the lawmaker here is Moses, not a modern legislator.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names an artwork of tesserae; the adjective, from Moses, describes the biblical law he delivered.

clue.text: Final letter in love game, perhaps

parts.note: love is a score of zero, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: perhaps hints the word could be in a different form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The last letter written in a tennis match scoreline, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: A nameless sentimental person, exuding fragrance

indicators.note: nameless means without a name, so the abbreviation for name is taken out

parts.note: taken as written
a romantic is a sentimental, idealistic person

explanation.surface: An anonymous softie wearing strong perfume.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the usual abbreviation for name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aromatic gives off a pleasant, spicy smell.

clue.text: Number on edge get together

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
taken as written
a verge is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A group of people standing on a ledge meet up.
explanation.definitionFit: To converge is to come together at one point, as people or lines do.

clue.text: Drug tins? Take one inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the following pair of words sits within the word for tins

parts.note: tins and cans are the same metal containers
to nab is to take or seize
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A curt instruction about a drug supply in tins: swallow one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' reads as an instruction to swallow, but it is the word for grab.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis is the drug made from the hemp plant, smoked or eaten for its effects.

clue.text: Fame of Wren on reassessment

indicators.note: a reassessment looks at things again and rearranges them, so the letters are re-ordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Christopher Wren's reputation being reconsidered by historians.
explanation.walkthrough: Wren is Sir Christopher Wren, architect of St Paul's Cathedral in London, whose fame fits the surface neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown is widespread acclaim and celebrity, the same thing as fame.

clue.text: Is a card shop involved? I go in for love potions

indicators.note: go in says a letter enters the other group of letters
involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a greetings-card shop sells love potions.
explanation.walkthrough: Add I to the eleven letters of the opening phrase, then rearrange all twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodisiacs are substances said to arouse sexual desire, named after Aphrodite.

clue.text: Takes out the fruit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: goes on romantic outings with someone
second meaning: the sweet brown fruit of a palm

explanation.surface: Someone removes the fruit from a bowl or box.
explanation.definitionFit: To date someone is to take them out socially; dates are also the sticky fruit of the date palm.

clue.text: Harp on about long time at children's home

indicators.note: about suggests moving the letters around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone nags at length in a care home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harp on' reads as a verb phrase for nagging; it is simply six letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: An orphanage is an institution that houses and raises children without parents.

clue.text: Image of money making an impression in church

definitions.text: Image of money making an impression in church

parts.words: Image of money making an impression
parts.note: surface reading: a picture of cash that impresses people

parts.words: money making an impression in church
parts.note: setter's reading: a slang word for money also names the engraved memorial plates in churches, and paper rubbed over one takes its impression

explanation.surface: A picture of cash that wows the congregation at church.
explanation.walkthrough: Brass is British slang for money and also the engraved metal memorial plates set into church floors; rubbing wax over paper on one copies the image.
explanation.definitionFit: The hobby produces a copied picture of a monumental plate by rubbing crayon over paper laid on it.

clue.text: Fashionable trend entails comic performing after group

indicators.note: after tells us the comic and performing pieces follow the group

parts.note: a band is a group of people or musicians
a wag is a joker or wit
a performer who is on is on stage

explanation.surface: A popular craze involves a comedian appearing after a band.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumping on the bandwagon means joining a popular movement or fashion.

clue.text: Resign from office in new shadow cabinet — shown out!

indicators.note: new suggests the remaining letters are made into a fresh arrangement
out tells us the letters of the word before it are removed

parts.note: taken as written
these letters are struck from the phrase

explanation.surface: An opposition spokesperson quits the shadow cabinet and is shown the door.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing S, H, O, W and N from the phrase leaves ADCABIET to rearrange. The shadow cabinet is the opposition party's team of would-be ministers in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: To abdicate is to renounce a throne or high post, giving up office.

clue.text: Stick to a tall thin person

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pole supporting climbing beans
second meaning: an informal name for a lanky person

explanation.surface: Stay loyal to a lanky individual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick to' reads as a verb phrase; Stick is a noun and to only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanpole is a garden cane, and by extension a jokey label for a very tall, skinny person.

clue.text: Doctor added: "Bring up the dessert!"

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor adds a request for the sweet course to be served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' poses as the speaker of the quoted line, but it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread pudding is a baked dessert of soaked bread with dried fruit and spice.

clue.text: Massacre programme right away without me

indicators.note: away means sent off, so the letter for right is dropped
without means lacking, so the letters of the following word are removed

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right; this letter is removed
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A brutal schedule is cut short, with the speaker taken out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the clue does not quite work: taking R and ME out of the word leaves POGRAM, with A where POGROM needs O. The setter seems to have slipped on the vowel.
explanation.definitionFit: A pogrom is an organised massacre of a persecuted group, originally of Jews in Tsarist Russia.

clue.text: After five let's daughter wander over the plains

indicators.note: after says the following material comes behind the numeral

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: to wander is to stray about, so the letters move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: After five o'clock, a parent lets their daughter roam the open grasslands.
explanation.definitionFit: The veld is the open grassland of southern Africa; veldts are such plains.

clue.text: Amusing or possibly poorly educated person

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could form something else when rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who is either entertaining or simply uneducated.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is an ignorant person, one lacking knowledge or schooling.

clue.text: Cook a sort of meat dish

indicators.note: to cook is also to fiddle or falsify, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to prepare a particular kind of meat dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like the definition, and fits the answer as a verb, but the noun definition sits at the end: Cook is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A roast is a joint of meat cooked in the oven, served as a main course.

clue.text: Complete with aperture

parts.note: W is a standard abbreviation for with
an aperture is an opening or hole

explanation.surface: Something finished and fitted with an opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole and complete both describe something entire, with nothing missing.

clue.text: Lacking principles needed for morning exam

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for the hours before noon
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A cheating student without scruples sitting an early test.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amoral has no moral standards at all, so is without principles.

clue.text: Pestered the animal initially every day

parts.note: the badger is the black-and-white burrowing mammal

indicators.note: initially tells us to take just the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of every
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: An animal pestered someone at the start of every day.
explanation.walkthrough: Badger, the animal, is also a verb meaning to nag, which the definition plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Badgered means harassed with repeated demands, the same as pestered.

clue.text: Chooses to put the French in English courts

indicators.note: in tells us one part is placed inside the others, between the two abbreviations

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
le is French for the
CTS is an abbreviation for courts

explanation.surface: Someone decides to move French people into English law courts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French' is the masculine French article.
explanation.definitionFit: To elect is to choose, whether a candidate by vote or a course of action.

clue.text: Waves to French friends about nuts at the start

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are turned around and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
amis is French for friends

explanation.surface: Someone waves to friends in France who are crazy about nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the start' places the rearranged nuts before the French friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsunamis are enormous sea waves caused by undersea earthquakes.
